title: Doughnut-chart Configuration
description: A doughnut/pie chart widget for visualizing proportional data as circular segments. Use this widget to display part-to-whole relationships, such as market share percentages, budget allocations, or category distributions. Supports multiple doughnut rings, pivot-based auto-generation of series from data columns, and configurable hole size (set to 0% for pie chart). Best for datasets with 2-8 categories where comparing relative proportions is important.

aiSelection.dataShape: A list of named parts with one numeric size each: dataseries[].sections[] gives a label and a value per slice. The parts are drawn as shares of their common total, so the numbers must be summable quantities (counts, amounts, durations) rather than rates or averages. An optional column bound to sections[].pivot splits the data into several rings, one per distinct value. Reads best with 2-8 slices.
useWhen: The question is what share each category has of a whole — split of production by program, share of downtime by cause, market share, budget allocation.
The numbers are parts of one total and the proportions matter more than the absolute values.
A pie chart is asked for rather than a doughnut: same widget, set dataseries[].settings.cutout to '0%'.
One ring per machine, site or period should be generated from a single column (bind it to sections[].pivot).
notFor: Comparing magnitudes across categories that are not shares of a total, or where there are more than about eight of them — use widget-linechart with dataseries[].type: 'bar'. Bars compare lengths, which the eye judges far better than angles.
Anything changing over time — a doughnut has no time dimension. Use widget-linechart.
A single value read against a minimum and maximum — use widget-gauge; a doughnut of one slice is always 100%.
Reading exact numbers rather than proportions — use widget-table, or a bar chart with dataseries[].styling.showValueLabels enabled.

title.title: Title
title.description: The main heading displayed above the doughnut chart. Use to describe what data is being visualized.

subTitle.title: Subtitle
subTitle.description: Secondary text displayed below the title. Use for additional context like time period, data source, or units.

columnLayout.title: Vertical Layout
columnLayout.description: When enabled, multiple doughnut charts are arranged vertically (stacked). When disabled, they are arranged horizontally (side by side).

dataseries.title: Doughnuts
dataseries.description: Array of doughnut chart configurations. Each entry creates a separate doughnut ring that can display different data or perspectives of the same dataset.

label.title: Label
label.description: The name identifier for this doughnut chart. Displayed in legends and tooltips.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Configuration options for the doughnut appearance and data processing.

cutout.title: Doghnut Hole Size
cutout.description: How big in percent should the hole in the middle of the doughnut be? Set to 0% for Pie Chart. Common values: 50% for standard doughnut, 70% for thin ring.

averageLatest.title: Average Latest Values
averageLatest.description: Calculate the average over the given number of newest rows. (If pivoted, then per each of the pivot dataseries.) If not specified then the latest value is shown without modification. Useful for smoothing volatile data.

sections.title: Data
sections.description: The table with columns to display as sections in the doughnut. Each section represents a slice of the chart.

items.title: Sections of the Doughnut
items.description: One doughnut ring will be drawn for the latest row in the chosen table. Each item in this array defines a section/slice.

name.title: Section Label
name.description: Display name for this doughnut section shown in tooltips and legends. Should be a chosen constant and usually not be assigned dynamically by a table column value.

value.title: Value
value.description: The numeric value determining the size of this section relative to other sections. Can be bound to a data column for dynamic updates.

color.title: Section Color
color.description: The fill color for this doughnut section. Should be a chosen constant and usually not be assigned dynamically by a table column value. Use distinct colors for each section to improve readability.

pivot.title: Split Data by
pivot.description: You can specify a column in the input data to autogenerate dataseries for each distinct entry in this column. E.g. if you have a table with columns [city, timestamp, temperature] and specify 'city' as split column, then you will get a doughnut for each city.
